title: EASE fast path literature evidence and bounded follow-up experiments

scope.purpose: Use primary papers and the official OpenPI implementation to identify bounded, no-large-model-retraining experiments for the fast-path insight.
not_claimed: The cited work does not prove complementary task preferences among Pi0/VLA paths.
The cited work does not prove runtime adaptive selection is useful in robot control.
Language-model or image-question-answering findings are not direct evidence for manipulation outcomes.

sources.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
source_facts: The paper routes images and language through the pretrained VLM weights, while robot state and noisy action tokens use a smaller action expert; the weight sets interact through self-attention.
The VLM Gemma depth is 18. Official OpenPI config uses SigLIP So400m/14 with depth 27 and Gemma 2B / Gemma 300M variants with depth 18.

Official inference code computes the observation prefix and KV cache once, then repeatedly processes the action suffix for flow integration steps; the paper reports 10 flow steps and separates image-encoder, observation-forward, and repeated action-forward costs.
sources.inference: Equal skipped-layer counts are not equal compute budgets across image encoding, the VLM observation prefix, and repeated action-expert execution. Branch allocation is a candidate for separate experiments only; it is not what the present V12 masks implement.

upstream_code_snapshot.scope: Architecture reference only. This upstream snapshot is not the local converted Triton runtime used by EASE experiments.

sources.title: ShortGPT: Layers in Large Language Models are More Redundant Than You Expect
source_facts: The paper defines Block Influence from adjacent-layer hidden-state similarity and reports non-uniform layer importance in Llama 2 and Baichuan2.
Removing some layers has small effects, while performance can fall sharply at particular layers as pruning increases.
Single attention-head effects vary across models without a universal redundancy ordering.
sources.inference: A one-layer exchange may be almost inert if it touches a redundant block, or cause broad damage if it touches a critical block; neither outcome guarantees category-specific complementarity.

sources.title: An Image is Worth 1/2 Tokens After Layer 2: Plug-and-Play Inference Acceleration for Large Vision-Language Models
source_facts: The paper reports inefficient attention computation over visual tokens in deep layers of several LVLMs.

Its training-free method ranks and prunes visual tokens at a chosen layer, with layer and prune ratio controls; reported experiments include image and video understanding and approximately 45% FLOPs reduction for example settings.
sources.inference: Visual computation can have a distinct redundancy profile from text processing, making visual-branch or visual-token allocation a plausible Pi0 follow-up. The paper changes token count, not VLA layer masks, so transfer remains an untested hypothesis.

sources.title: Task-specific Compression for Multi-task Language Models using Attribution-based Pruning
source_facts: The paper uses attribution to identify task-important neurons and constructs task-specific pruned language models without additional training.
It evaluates six NLU datasets and reports an unseen-domain setting.
sources.inference: A task ID or instruction category can be frozen as a static route-selection signal after discovery. This only motivates testing the selector; the paper does not establish VLA complementarity or practical latency gains from arbitrary sparsity.

why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.claim: The one-layer perturbation can be too small to change task outcomes, or large but non-selective.
why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.status: inference_for_vla; not directly tested by cited work

why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.claim: The same layer count does not imply the same saved compute because Pi0 has a 27-layer visual encoder, an 18-layer VLM/expert stack, prefix caching, and repeated action-suffix inference.
why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.status: architecture fact plus inference from official source

why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.claim: A whole-block V12 mask perturbs both image-token and language-token representations inside the observation prefix, but does not prune the action expert. Therefore these experiments do not establish preferences among AE layers, and a null result cannot rule out AE-path preferences.
why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.status: local implementation fact plus inference; task-category interaction remains unverified

why_single_layer_exchange_may_not_be_rob.claim: Task-specific pruning in other model families motivates a separately validated task-conditioned route, but discovery-set choices cannot count as confirmation.

proposals.question: At matched per-action compute, do the current observation-prefix mask path, a new image-encoder mask, or a new action-expert suffix mask have different task-category preferences?
controls: Same Pi0 checkpoint, preprocessing, normalization, action horizon, flow-step count, environment settings, and paired task/initial-state cases.
Match actual executed FLOPs or profiled compute per output using call counts and sequence shapes; skipped-layer counts alone are not a budget match.
Do not alter the existing queued 720-case local-mask search or reuse its confirmation cases for this independent proposal.

The current mask is not SigLIP-only, language-only, or AE-only: it skips VLM prefix hidden updates for the combined image-plus-language sequence, retains K/V shells, and applies residual compensation.
Image-encoder and action-expert masks are new experimental mechanisms requiring their own code revision, execution audit, and immutable manifest; no results from the current V12 masks validate them.
The 90% reference-FLOPs target is a proposal value, not a registered budget.
proposals.discovery: Four predeclared categories (Spatial, Object, Goal, Long), 10 tasks/category, 2 initial states/task; select at most one candidate pair from the three branch paths.
proposals.confirmation: Freeze masks and category contrast; use new initial states, at least 10 tasks/category and 4 unseen states/task.
proposals.primary_metric: Paired success-rate interaction between the predeclared task-category pair, with task-clustered 95% bootstrap intervals.
secondary_metrics: native-policy wall time per executed action
acceptance and Full-fallback rates when the runtime exposes them
proposals.positive_rule: Proposed criterion only: opposite A-versus-B preference of at least 10 percentage points in each category with both task-clustered 95% intervals excluding zero; each path would also need to meet a separately preregistered Full non-inferiority margin and show measured latency reduction. These thresholds are not in the current manifest.
proposals.falsification: No reversed category preference, unstable independent replication, failure of the Full non-inferiority margin, or no measured speed gain means this does not establish a useful complementary fast-path pair.

proposals.question: At matched compute, does bypassing attention residual sub-blocks versus MLP residual sub-blocks produce reproducible category-specific preferences?
controls: Freeze branch and candidate layer positions before confirmation; no large-model retraining.
Use profiler-measured executed FLOPs or latency to match budgets (target approximately 10% of reference compute); do not equate one attention block with one MLP block by count.
Limit discovery to 12 preregistered layer-range combinations and select at most one pair.

The current EASE Backend skips whole VLM blocks using KV-only computation plus residual compensation; it does not use the lower-level attention/FFN skip arguments. This is a new sub-block mechanism and needs a separate runtime revision and manifest.
The approximately 10% compute target and 12 candidate layer ranges are proposals, not preregistered or frozen in the current queue.
proposals.discovery_and_confirmation: Use the same separate discovery/confirmation scheme as proposal A with paired task/initial-state cases.
proposals.primary_metric: The preregistered path-by-category success-rate interaction, clustered by task.
proposals.positive_rule: Proposed criterion only: independent confirmation would reproduce opposite category preferences at a newly frozen minimum effect and latency criterion; neither is registered for this future mechanism.
proposals.falsification: An overall attention-versus-MLP difference without an independently reproduced category interaction supports only a general sub-module effect, not task-specific complementarity.

proposals.question: After a complementary pair is independently identified, does selecting a fixed path by known task category outperform the best single fixed path?
conditions: fixed path A on every case
fixed path B on every case
controls: Only run after a path pair is confirmed in A, B, or the current frozen local-search branch.
Freeze one category-to-path mapping on discovery data; confirmation uses new initial states and the same per-case compute budget.
Selector reads only the known task/suite ID before inference; it cannot use images, state, trajectory history, or within-episode phase.
proposals.confirmation: At least 10 tasks per category and 4 new initial states per task; compare all four conditions on paired cases.
proposals.primary_metric: Paired success-rate gain of the frozen router over the discovery-selected best fixed path, with task-clustered 95% bootstrap interval.
proposals.positive_rule: Proposed criterion only: confirmation would need at least a 5 percentage-point gain, a task-cluster bootstrap interval lower bound above zero, and a matched per-case budget. These are not currently registered.
proposals.falsification: If routing does not beat the best fixed path, or A dominates B across categories, use one fixed path; do not claim task-level selection benefit. A positive result still does not establish within-episode adaptation.

phase_followup_boundary.recommendation: Only after static complementarity is confirmed, consider a separate new runtime revision testing a fixed route schedule keyed by known flow timestep while keeping total flow steps and total path-compute budget constant. Test early/late and reversed schedules on independent cases. This is not part of current V12 masks.
phase_followup_boundary.not_established_by_static_task_router: Episode-phase detection, online path selection, transition overhead, and a runtime adaptive policy.

local_runtime_contract.evidence_source: Read-only source trace of preparations/ease_insights_20261103/vlm/backend.py and policy.py, inherited preparations/idea1_v3/policy.py, preparations/idea1_v2_2/pi0_adapter.py, policies/realtime-vla-flash/scripts/spec/triton/pi0_infer.py, and both frozen result manifests.
local_runtime_contract.mask_target: Observation-prefix VLM transformer only. The prefix sequence contains projected image tokens plus language prompt embeddings.
local_runtime_contract.image_encoder: Runs fully in prepare; V12 skip mask is not applied to the image encoder.
local_runtime_contract.skipped_vlm_layer_semantics: For one-based layers 1-17, a skipped block computes the original-index K/V shell but omits Q, attention-output, and FFN hidden-state updates. The hidden state then receives the mask-specific residual compensation/extrapolation saved from that path. Layer 18 is K/V-only in this implementation and is not an eligible hidden-update skip.
local_runtime_contract.action_expert: sample receives no layer mask. Each flow integration step executes all 18 action-expert layers.
local_runtime_contract.per_request_difference: The VLM path uses the fixed V12 mask on Fast calls and recomputes/captures masked-layer residuals on Full refreshes. The action expert remains full-depth; Fast uses D=2 integration steps and Full refresh uses D=10.
local_runtime_contract.schedule: Full-D10 refresh followed by up to two Fast-D2 requests.
local_runtime_contract.authority: The local frozen manifests and their source-file SHA256 entries govern experimental implementation identity. The pinned upstream GitHub commit is a separate architecture reference.
